registry_rules: Only an active adapter row can validate a did or project it to did_core_id. DID syntax alone never admits a method.
project is a method-defined semantic transform over a canonical bare did, not generic string concatenation or prefix removal. Receivers compare the complete projected did_core_id byte-for-byte.

Every adapter validates method-native control, deactivation, currentness and history evidence according to its trust profile before returning a verified projection. Unknown methods and unknown adapter versions fail closed.

A new did is an update of an existing principal or service only when the same active adapter projects it to the identical did_core_id. A method or core change creates a new identity and cannot inherit authorization through a continuity assertion.
DID URLs are constructed and compared from the verified did under the adapter's DID URL rules. A did_core_id is never used as a DID URL base.

No adapter exposes expand or core_to_did. Even when a method-specific suffix appears reversible, an isolated did_core_id cannot create resolution authority; the required did or did_url arrives through did-evidence-boundary-registry.json.

A did is a canonical bare DID and therefore contains no path, query or fragment. Each active adapter deterministically emits method_history_head, version_id and service_resolution_event_ref according to its registered rules, including synthetic values for methods without native history.

For a generic Event proof, the verifier extracts the canonical bare did base from proof.verification_method, validates the active adapter and key at the cited accepted-at method history, projects that did, and compares the resulting did_core_id to executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery are the only registered special admissions and never convert current DID control into generic human PCR authority.

A principal resolution update is admitted only in its derived identity-control Realm and only when one exact head_eq precondition guards ak:cell:ak.component.identity.resolution.v1:null. The guarded whole resolution_projection MUST equal the accepted current cell; predecessor event/history coordinates come only from that signed precondition, never from payload mirrors.

Exactly one active adapter row per human_principal_anchor method declares registration_anchor_kind, and that value is the sole discriminator of the closed principal-registration-anchor union. A human principal is registered, given PCR genesis and later replayed from a portable account_device_control root only through the branch that value selects. did:web carries human_principal_anchor=false: ordinary WebPKI authenticates a TLS endpoint rather than the served DID document body, so a did:web registration produces no portable offline-verifiable publication proof. A human registration naming an ineligible method MUST fail closed with unsupported_did_method at schema and role admission, before any method parser, history replay or registry write. Restoring did:web as a human anchor requires a newly registered publication-proof or independent-witness trust model with its own threat model and conformance vectors; it MUST NOT return through a test fixture, an optional sidecar member or a locally widened allowlist.

predecessor_rules: precondition.value equals the accepted current resolution_projection field for field
payload.next is a method-valid successor of precondition.value.method_history_head

checks: the response carries none of principal_control_realm_id, principal_genesis_event, principal_genesis_receipt, current_resolution_event, predecessor_resolution_events or accepted_seal; any such member is a schema violation on this surface
projection_attestation.attestation.principal_id == principal_id and projection_attestation.attestation.station_id == station_id
projection_attestation.attestation.resolution_projection equals resolution_projection field for field
projection_attestation.attestation.method_history_evidence_digest == sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of method_history_evidence
projection_attestation.proof signs the registered attestation transcript, proof.created_at == attestation.issued_at, and attestation.issued_at < attestation.expires_at
projection_attestation.proof.verification_method resolves to an assertion-capable key under the current verified method history of station_id
project(resolution_projection.did) == principal_id
method_history_evidence boundary and currentness validate under the adapter selected by resolution_projection.did
principal_genesis_event.kind == ak.realm.create and principal_genesis_event is resolution head 0
principal_genesis_event.actor_id == principal_id
principal_genesis_event.payload.object.purpose is principal_control, agent_control or applet_managed_control
project(principal_genesis_event.payload.object.initial_resolution.did) == principal_id
derive_identity_control_realm(principal_genesis_event) == principal_control_realm_id
every post-genesis event is ak.identity.resolution.update with actor_id == principal_id and realm_id == principal_control_realm_id

if current_resolution_event is principal_genesis_event then predecessor_resolution_events is empty; otherwise predecessor_resolution_events[0] is the current Event's guarded immediate predecessor when history_depth is nonzero

the supplied resolution events form a contiguous immediate-predecessor segment backward from current_resolution_event under the exact guarded whole-cell values; the segment never exceeds request history_depth items and never skips an intermediate Event

history_complete is true exactly when the segment terminates at principal_genesis_event or at the exclusive request after_resolution_event_ref ancestor; otherwise history_complete is false, next_audit_cursor equals value.resolution_event_ref in the exact head_eq precondition of the oldest supplied Event (its guarded immediate predecessor), and omitted history is never treated as absent
accepted_seal.realm_id == principal_control_realm_id and accepted_seal recursively covers both principal_genesis_event.event_digest and current_resolution_event.event_digest
the registered resolution reducer applied to current_resolution_event yields the response's current resolution projection and project(did) == principal_id
method_history_evidence boundary and currentness validate under the adapter selected by that current resolution projection's did

portable.relocation_rule: A successor whose canonical host-and-path differs from the accepted predecessor is valid only when the predecessor's effective portable value is true and every method-native successor check succeeds. Missing or false rejects relocation; setting portable=true only in the relocating successor cannot authorize that same relocation.

watchers.rule: The adapter validates and retains watchers as method-native canonical data, but v1 never uses it for authorization, admission, controller selection, witness quorum, freshness, routing or policy. Unknown shape still fails under the method parser; presence, absence or contents cannot grant authority.

adapters.method_history_head_rule: sha256:<lowercase-hex SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of the verified current did:webvh log entry>
adapters.version_id_rule: The exact method-native versionId of that same verified current did:webvh log entry, serialized as a non-empty string.
adapters.service_resolution_event_ref_rule: did-webvh-entry-sha256:<the same 64 lowercase hex octets carried by method_history_head after sha256:>

adapters.method_history_head_rule: sha256:<lowercase-hex SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of the verified current DID Document>
adapters.version_id_rule: synthetic-jcs-sha256:<the same 64 lowercase hex octets carried by method_history_head after sha256:>
adapters.service_resolution_event_ref_rule: did-web-document-sha256:<the same 64 lowercase hex octets carried by method_history_head after sha256:>

adapters.method_history_head_rule: sha256:<lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of canonical did>
adapters.version_id_rule: synthetic-did-sha256:<the same 64 lowercase hex octets carried by method_history_head after sha256:>
adapters.service_resolution_event_ref_rule: did-key-did-sha256:<the same 64 lowercase hex octets carried by method_history_head after sha256:>
